title: Malerkotla Is Spared Within a Shared Khalsa Order

blocks.text: This page opens with scriptural praise for the transforming company of the saintly, then applies that moral frame to policy. Muslims remain within territories now shaped by Sikh power, but the Pathans of Malerkotla are explicitly spared in keeping with the Guru's remembered word and the distinctive moral status attached to that house.

From there the poem moves into negotiated governance: tribute, shared tracts, and coordinated misl control replace indiscriminate devastation. Even where conquest has widened, not every place is treated as a target for the same punishment.
The result is a more nuanced picture of Khalsa sovereignty. Mercy, obligation, common territorial arrangements, and alliance all sit alongside the force that made such arrangements possible.
